milestones.title: Outcome 1: Users can self-serve trusted data
milestones.description: Outcome: analysts and service teams can find, understand and access trusted data without raising a ticket. Measure: 50% fewer access requests to the data team; catalogue used weekly by 300+ users.

milestones.title: Outcome 2: Data is reliable and well governed
milestones.description: Outcome: teams trust the numbers because quality issues are caught early and ownership is clear. Measure: 90% of critical datasets with quality checks; data incidents resolved within 2 working days.

milestones.title: Outcome 3: Faster insight with AI-assisted analysis
milestones.description: Outcome: users get answers from data faster with safe, governed AI tools. Measure: median time from question to answer down 40%; 200+ monthly active users of AI tools.

stories.title: Search datasets by keyword
stories.body:
As an analyst, I want to search datasets by name, description and tags so that I can find relevant data quickly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A search box on the catalogue accepts a keyword and returns matching datasets
- [ ] Matches include dataset name, description and tags, case-insensitively
- [ ] Results update as the user types, or after they submit the search
- [ ] An empty or no-match result explains that nothing was found and how to refine the search

Parent epic: #8

stories.title: Filter datasets by domain and owner
stories.body:
As a service team member, I want to filter datasets by domain and owner so that I can narrow results to my area.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Users can filter the catalogue by domain and by owner, including after a keyword search
- [ ] Filters can be combined, and the result count updates to match
- [ ] Applied filters are visible and can be cleared individually or all at once
- [ ] The domain and owner lists only include values that exist in the catalogue

Parent epic: #8

stories.title: Show key metadata in search results
stories.body:
As an analyst, I want search results to show owner, last refreshed date and domain so that I can judge relevance without opening each dataset.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each result shows the dataset name, domain, owner and last refreshed date
- [ ] Missing metadata is shown as 'Not recorded' rather than left blank
- [ ] Results remain scannable on a typical laptop viewport without horizontal scrolling

Parent epic: #8

stories.title: View dataset schema and ownership
stories.body:
As an analyst, I want to see a dataset's schema, owner and refresh schedule on one page so that I can decide if it is fit for my work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The dataset page shows name, description, owner, steward, domain and refresh schedule
- [ ] The schema lists field names, types and descriptions where available
- [ ] The page is reachable from a search result
- [ ] A dataset that cannot be found returns a clear not-found message

Parent epic: #10

stories.title: Preview sample rows
stories.body:
As an analyst, I want to preview sample rows for a dataset so that I can check the data looks as I expect before requesting access.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The dataset page shows a limited sample of rows (for example the first 10)
- [ ] Sample columns match the published schema
- [ ] If the user does not have permission to preview, the page explains this and does not show row values
- [ ] Sensitive fields already tagged are masked in the preview

Parent epic: #10

stories.title: Show dataset lineage summary
stories.body:
As a data owner, I want a lineage summary on the dataset page so that users understand where the data comes from.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The dataset page shows immediate upstream sources and immediate downstream consumers where known
- [ ] Each lineage item links to the related dataset page when that dataset is in the catalogue
- [ ] If lineage is not yet recorded, the page states that rather than showing an empty diagram

Parent epic: #10

stories.title: Create and edit glossary terms
stories.body:
As a data steward, I want to create and edit business glossary terms so that we have shared definitions of key terms.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A steward can create a term with a name, definition and optional synonyms
- [ ] A steward can edit or retire a term, and a history of changes is retained
- [ ] Duplicate term names are rejected with a clear error
- [ ] Only stewards or glossary editors can change terms; other users can view them

Parent epic: #9

stories.title: Link glossary terms to datasets
stories.body:
As an analyst, I want glossary terms to be linked to datasets so that I can understand what a field or dataset means.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A steward can link a glossary term to a dataset or to a specific field
- [ ] The dataset page lists linked terms with their definitions
- [ ] The glossary term page lists the datasets and fields it is linked to
- [ ] Removing a link does not delete the term or the dataset

Parent epic: #9

stories.title: Search the business glossary
stories.body:
As a service team member, I want to search the glossary by term or synonym so that I can look up definitions without asking the data team.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Users can search glossary terms by name, synonym or words in the definition
- [ ] Results show the term name, a short definition and any linked datasets
- [ ] A no-match result explains that no term was found

Parent epic: #9

stories.title: Submit an access request with purpose and duration
stories.body:
As an analyst, I want to request access to a dataset with a stated purpose and duration so that the owner can make an informed decision.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The form requires a purpose and a requested duration (start and end, or a period)
- [ ] The request is stored against the dataset and the requester
- [ ] A confirmation is shown, including a request reference
- [ ] Incomplete forms cannot be submitted and missing fields are highlighted

Parent epic: #11

stories.title: Track my access request status
stories.body:
As a service team member, I want to see the status of my access requests so that I know when I can start using the data.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A requester can see a list of their requests with status (submitted, approved, rejected, expired)
- [ ] Each item shows the dataset, date submitted and current status
- [ ] The list updates when an owner makes a decision

Parent epic: #11

stories.title: Request access from the dataset page
stories.body:
As an analyst, I want to request access from the dataset detail page so that I do not have to raise a separate ticket.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The dataset page has a request-access action that opens the access request form with the dataset pre-selected
- [ ] If the user already has active access, the page says so instead of inviting a duplicate request
- [ ] If a request is already pending, the page links to that request rather than creating another

Parent epic: #11

stories.title: Notify owners of new access requests
stories.body:
As a data owner, I want to be notified when someone requests access to my dataset so that I can respond promptly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a request is submitted, the dataset owner receives an email notification
- [ ] The notification includes the requester, dataset, purpose, duration and a link to review it
- [ ] If no owner is recorded, the request is routed to a fallback steward or data-team inbox

Parent epic: #12

stories.title: Approve or reject access requests
stories.body:
As a data owner, I want to approve or reject a request with a reason so that there is a clear audit trail.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An owner can approve or reject a pending request and must provide a reason when rejecting
- [ ] The decision, actor, timestamp and reason are stored and cannot be silently altered
- [ ] Only the dataset owner or a designated delegate can decide on the request
- [ ] A request cannot be decided twice; a second attempt explains it is already closed

Parent epic: #12

stories.title: Notify requesters of the decision
stories.body:
As an analyst, I want to be notified when my request is approved or rejected so that I know the outcome without chasing the owner.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The requester receives an email when the request is approved or rejected
- [ ] A rejection email includes the owner's reason
- [ ] An approval email states the access duration
- [ ] The request status in the requester's list matches the notification

Parent epic: #12

stories.title: Auto-provision warehouse permissions on approval
stories.body:
As a data owner, I want approved requests to grant warehouse permissions automatically so that I do not have to provision access by hand.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a request is approved, the corresponding warehouse permission is granted for the requester and dataset
- [ ] A failure to provision is recorded, the owner is notified, and the request is marked as needing attention
- [ ] Successful provisioning is reflected on the request record with a timestamp

Parent epic: #13

stories.title: Auto-revoke access when duration ends
stories.body:
As an analyst, I want my access to be revoked automatically when the agreed duration ends so that unused access is not left open.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When the approved duration ends, warehouse permission is revoked automatically
- [ ] The requester is notified before expiry and again when access is revoked
- [ ] The request record shows an expired or revoked status and the revoke timestamp
- [ ] A failed revoke is logged and raised to the platform team

Parent epic: #13

stories.title: Audit log of permission changes
stories.body:
As a platform engineer, I want a log of permission grants and revokes so that we can audit who had access and when.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every grant and revoke is logged with actor or system process, dataset, user, timestamp and related request
- [ ] Authorised auditors can search the log by user, dataset and date range
- [ ] Log entries cannot be edited or deleted through the application

Parent epic: #13

stories.title: Define quality rules for a dataset
stories.body:
As a data steward, I want to define freshness, completeness and validity rules for a dataset so that quality issues are caught automatically.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A steward can add freshness, completeness and validity rules to a dataset, each with a threshold or condition
- [ ] Rules are saved against the dataset and can be viewed on its quality settings
- [ ] Invalid rule configuration (for example a missing threshold) is rejected with a clear error

Parent epic: #14

stories.title: Run quality rules after each refresh
stories.body:
As a data engineer, I want quality rules to run on a schedule after each refresh so that checks keep pace with the data.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Enabled rules run automatically after a dataset refresh, or on a configured schedule if no refresh event exists
- [ ] Each run stores a pass or fail result, the time of the run and a short summary
- [ ] A failed or skipped run is visible to the steward and does not block later runs

Parent epic: #14

stories.title: Enable or disable quality rules
stories.body:
As a data steward, I want to enable or disable rules per dataset so that I can tune checks without a code change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A steward can enable or disable an individual rule without deleting it
- [ ] Disabled rules are not executed and are clearly marked as inactive
- [ ] The change is recorded with the actor and timestamp

Parent epic: #14

stories.title: Alert owners when a quality rule fails
stories.body:
As a dataset owner, I want Slack and email alerts when a quality rule fails so that I can investigate before users are affected.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a rule fails, the dataset owner is alerted by email and, if configured, Slack
- [ ] The alert names the dataset, the rule, the failure summary and a link to the result
- [ ] Repeated failures of the same rule within a short window are grouped so owners are not flooded

Parent epic: #15

stories.title: Configure quality alert recipients
stories.body:
As a dataset owner, I want to choose who is notified and how so that the right people are reached without unnecessary noise.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An owner can set email and Slack recipients for quality alerts on their dataset
- [ ] Recipients can be added or removed, and a dataset can have more than one recipient
- [ ] Alerts are only sent on the channels that have been configured

Parent epic: #15

stories.title: Show a quality score on the dataset page
stories.body:
As an analyst, I want to see a quality score on the dataset page so that I can judge whether to trust the data before I use it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The dataset page shows a quality score based on recent rule results
- [ ] The score explains how it was calculated (for example rules passed versus failed in the last period)
- [ ] If no rules have been run, the page states that a score is not yet available

Parent epic: #16

stories.title: Cross-domain quality dashboard
stories.body:
As a data lead, I want a cross-domain quality dashboard so that I can see which areas need attention.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A dashboard lists datasets with their latest quality score, grouped or filterable by domain
- [ ] Users can sort or filter to find failing or stale checks
- [ ] Each row links through to the dataset page

Parent epic: #16

stories.title: Assign owners and stewards to datasets
stories.body:
As a data lead, I want every critical dataset to have a named owner and steward so that responsibilities are clear.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A data lead can assign an owner and a steward to a dataset from the organisation directory
- [ ] The dataset page and registry list show the current owner and steward
- [ ] Critical datasets missing an owner or steward are identifiable in the registry

Parent epic: #17

stories.title: Sync owners and stewards from the HR directory
stories.body:
As a data steward, I want owner and steward details to stay in sync with the HR directory so that records stay current when people change roles or leave.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Owner and steward names, contact details and status are refreshed from the HR directory on a schedule
- [ ] If a recorded owner or steward has left, the dataset is flagged as needing a new assignment
- [ ] Directory sync failures are logged and visible to the platform team

Parent epic: #17

stories.title: Stewardship queue for incomplete datasets
stories.body:
As a data steward, I want a queue of datasets missing descriptions, classifications or reviews so that I can work through gaps systematically.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A steward sees a queue of datasets they are responsible for that are missing a description, classification or scheduled review
- [ ] Each item states what is missing and links to the dataset
- [ ] Completing the missing work removes the item from the queue

Parent epic: #18

stories.title: Track overdue stewardship tasks
stories.body:
As a data lead, I want to see overdue stewardship tasks so that I can follow up where ownership is slipping.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tasks past their review or completion date are marked overdue
- [ ] A data lead can view overdue tasks across their domain, with steward and dataset
- [ ] The view can be filtered by domain or steward

Parent epic: #18

stories.title: Tag sensitive fields on a dataset
stories.body:
As a data steward, I want to tag personal and sensitive fields on a dataset so that downstream users handle them correctly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A steward can tag fields as personal, sensitive or another agreed classification
- [ ] Tagged fields are visible on the dataset schema and in sample previews (masked where required)
- [ ] Tags can be changed or removed, and the change is recorded

Parent epic: #19

stories.title: Suggest sensitive field tags from patterns
stories.body:
As a data steward, I want suggested tags from pattern detection so that I can classify fields faster and more consistently.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The system suggests classifications for fields that match known patterns (for example email, postcode, NHS number)
- [ ] Suggestions are presented for a steward to accept or dismiss; they are not applied automatically
- [ ] Accepted suggestions become field tags; dismissed suggestions are not shown again for that field unless the schema changes

Parent epic: #19

stories.title: Apply retention periods to datasets
stories.body:
As a data owner, I want to apply a retention period to a dataset so that we do not keep data longer than we should.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An owner can set a retention period on a dataset (for example 12 or 24 months from last activity or a fixed end date)
- [ ] The retention period is shown on the dataset page
- [ ] A change to the retention period is recorded with the actor and reason

Parent epic: #20

stories.title: Flag data overdue for deletion
stories.body:
As a data steward, I want to be flagged when data is overdue for deletion so that we can act before we breach policy.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Datasets past their retention date are flagged as overdue for deletion
- [ ] The steward and owner are notified, with a link to review the dataset
- [ ] The flag is cleared once deletion is confirmed or the retention period is legitimately extended

Parent epic: #20

stories.title: Ask a question in plain English
stories.body:
As an analyst, I want to ask a question in plain English against curated datasets so that I can get SQL without writing it from scratch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can type a natural-language question and receive generated SQL for a curated dataset
- [ ] The assistant indicates which dataset or datasets it used
- [ ] If the question cannot be interpreted, the user sees a clear message and a prompt to rephrase

Parent epic: #21

stories.title: Review and edit generated SQL
stories.body:
As an analyst, I want to see and edit the generated SQL before it runs so that I can correct or refine the query.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Generated SQL is shown before execution and can be edited by the user
- [ ] The edited SQL is what is run when the user confirms
- [ ] The original generated SQL is retained for comparison

Parent epic: #21

stories.title: Limit the assistant to curated datasets
stories.body:
As a data engineer, I want the assistant limited to catalogue-curated datasets so that users cannot query unmanaged tables.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The assistant can only generate queries against datasets marked as curated in the catalogue
- [ ] A question that requires an unmanaged table is refused with an explanation
- [ ] The allowed dataset list is taken from the catalogue, not hard-coded

Parent epic: #21

stories.title: Enforce access permissions on generated queries
stories.body:
As a security officer, I want generated queries to respect the user's existing access permissions so that the assistant cannot bypass access controls.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A generated or edited query is checked against the user's dataset permissions before it runs
- [ ] Queries that include datasets the user cannot access are blocked
- [ ] The permission check uses the same source of truth as warehouse access

Parent epic: #22

stories.title: Apply cost and row limits to generated queries
stories.body:
As a platform engineer, I want cost and row limits on generated queries so that a bad prompt cannot run an expensive query.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Queries are subject to a configurable row limit and estimated-cost ceiling
- [ ] A query that would exceed a limit is not executed
- [ ] Limits can be adjusted by a platform engineer without a code release

Parent epic: #22

stories.title: Explain when a query is blocked by guardrails
stories.body:
As an analyst, I want a clear error when a question is blocked by guardrails so that I understand why I cannot run it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a query is blocked, the user is told whether the reason was permissions, cost, row limit or another guardrail
- [ ] The message suggests a next step (for example request access, narrow the question)
- [ ] The blocked attempt is logged for audit without exposing data the user cannot see

Parent epic: #22

stories.title: Show SQL, sources and caveats with answers
stories.body:
As an analyst, I want to see the SQL, datasets used and caveats alongside every answer so that I can trust and explain the result.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every answer shows the SQL that was run, the datasets used and any caveats (for example incomplete data or failed quality checks)
- [ ] Dataset names link to the catalogue page
- [ ] This explanation is available for both successful answers and answers based on partial results

Parent epic: #23

stories.title: Chart numeric answers
stories.body:
As a service team member, I want a chart of the answer when the question is numeric so that I can share the insight quickly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When the result is a numeric series or comparison, a simple chart is shown alongside the table
- [ ] The user can download or copy the chart and the underlying data
- [ ] If a chart is not appropriate, only the table is shown, with no broken visualisation

Parent epic: #23

stories.title: Provide a gateway API with per-team keys
stories.body:
As a platform engineer, I want a single gateway API with per-team keys so that teams use approved models through one route.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Teams can be issued a gateway API key that authenticates requests to the single approved endpoint
- [ ] Requests without a valid key are rejected
- [ ] Keys can be rotated or revoked without changing the endpoint URL

Parent epic: #24

stories.title: Route requests to the appropriate model
stories.body:
As a platform engineer, I want to route requests to the right model by team or use case so that we can manage cost and capability.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The gateway routes a request to a model based on team and use-case configuration
- [ ] A platform engineer can change routing rules without a code release
- [ ] Unsupported models or misconfigured routes return a clear error and are logged

Parent epic: #24

stories.title: Dashboard of AI usage and spend
stories.body:
As a data lead, I want a dashboard of usage and spend by team and model so that I can manage AI costs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A dashboard shows request volume and estimated spend, breakable by team and by model, for a chosen date range
- [ ] Figures are based on gateway logs, not on informal estimates
- [ ] Authorised leads can export the breakdown

Parent epic: #25

stories.title: Spend alerts per team
stories.body:
As a platform engineer, I want to set and monitor spend alerts per team so that unexpected usage is caught early.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A platform engineer can set a spend threshold per team
- [ ] When a team exceeds the threshold in the current period, the engineer and team contact are notified
- [ ] Alerts can be acknowledged, and thresholds can be updated

Parent epic: #25
